purpose: Route each task to a level and the agents that may take it

question.value:
Classify this task: its kind of work, its risk, and three yes/no properties.

Kind of work: feature, bug fix (bugfix), refactor, test, docs, chore, sync, spec, design, implementation plan (plan), review of someone else's work (review), research, analysis, art or visual design (art), or repair of a failed integration or build (repair). Answer unknown if you cannot tell.

Risk is how much damage the change could do if it is wrong. Judge it separately from how hard the work is, and from how well the task is written.
- High risk: merging and publishing, CI gating, crash and session recovery, git branch handling, database migrations and stored data, authentication, permissions and secrets, money and live trading, deleting anything. Treat it as very high when a mistake would be hard to undo or would reach outside the repository.
- Medium risk: ordinary changes to shared code that other work depends on.
- Low risk: docs, UI copy, isolated components and tests, where a mistake is visible and cheap to undo.
When a task touches several areas, go by the riskiest. When you can't tell, answer unknown.

"Narrow" means the requirements are settled and the files to change are named or obvious. "Covered by a test" means an existing or specified test checks the result. Work that needs manual or end-to-end verification is not covered.

Needs deep reasoning: judge this from the task itself, not from how it was labelled or what level was asked for. It holds only when the work needs advanced mathematics or unusually hard reasoning. A big task is not a deep task, and neither is a risky one.
Clearly harder: research that is clearly harder than ordinary research.

label.value: Kind given by whoever filed it

value.description: What kind of work the task is.

then.value: Deep, high effort, because the work needs advanced mathematics or unusually hard reasoning.

default.value: The level is the one the routing document gives this kind of work.

then.value: Tests, docs, chores and syncs don't go above Standard, so the level asked for was lowered to Standard, high effort.

default.value: Asking for Deep is not enough to get it: this task does not need advanced mathematics or unusually hard reasoning, so it gets Complex, high effort.

detail.value: The level whoever filed the task asked for was used.
The level asked for isn't available, so the nearest available level below it was used, but never below what the other rules give.
A bug fix that has already failed once for a real reason moves up to Complex, high effort.

then.value: Very high risk work is at least Complex, medium effort.

default.value: Medium and high risk work, and very high risk work that is narrow and covered by a test, are at least Standard, high effort.

detail.value: Very high risk work that is narrow and covered by a test needs only Standard, high effort, not Complex.
The risk could not be worked out, so it counts as medium.
The kind of work could not be worked out, so it gets at least Standard, high effort, and stays on Claude or Codex.
High and very high risk work goes only to Claude or Codex. Medium risk work goes to Claude or Codex, and to a local model only when it is narrow, covered by a test, and Standard.
Design and planning go to Claude first, and to Codex only when Claude can't take them.
Low risk work that is narrow and covered by a test goes to a local model first, to save Claude and Codex usage.
Art and visual design go to Codex, and wait for it rather than going elsewhere.
Repairs to a failed integration or build never go to a local model.
